quizName: DMV Practice Test #6 15 Questions • Passing Score 12

questions.question: If you must brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, you should:

options.text: Brake first then swerve, or swerve first then brake.
Brake and swerve at the same time.
Choose to do only one: brake or swerve.
Only use the front brake and do not swerve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake first then swerve, or swerve first then brake.
questions.explanation: Do the actions separately. Do not brake while swerving because your motorcycle may tip over.

questions.question: A good face shield should NOT:

options.text: Let you see clearly to both sides.

questions.explanation: A face shield must allow air to pass through. If it is airtight, it will fog up and make it hard to see.

questions.question: To lower crash risk, do all of the following EXCEPT:

options.text: Be ready to react to hazards.

questions.explanation: You must be visible and signal your plans clearly. Watch for hazards ahead and be ready to react. Do not rely on hoping others see you.

questions.question: If one of your tires goes flat while riding, you should:

options.text: Gently apply the brake on the tire that is not flat.
Speed up to leave the road quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gently apply the brake on the tire that is not flat.
questions.explanation: Ease off the throttle and keep the bike straight as you slow down. If you must brake, slowly apply the brake of the tire that is not flat.

questions.question: When braking, you should only use the rear brake.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes whenever you slow down or stop.

questions.question: When riding at night, do all of the following EXCEPT:

options.text: Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to help you see.
Ride only in the left part of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride only in the left part of your lane.
questions.explanation: Use your high beam, use other vehicles' headlights to help you see, and wear reflective clothing. Change your lane position as needed to see, be seen, and stay safe.

questions.question: As you slow or stop, you should:
questions.explanation: Shift down through the gears as you slow. Stay in first gear while stopped so you can move quickly if needed.

questions.question: Where is a motorcycle most likely to conflict with other traffic?
questions.explanation: The biggest risk is at intersections where other vehicles may cross your path. Stay alert at these locations.

questions.question: Most motorcycle crashes happen on short trips.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes occur on short trips of less than five miles, often within the first few minutes of riding.

questions.question: If your rear wheel locks while braking on a surface with good grip, you should:

options.text: Keep it locked until you stop completely.
Release the rear brake and use only the front brake.
Release the rear brake, then quickly apply it again.
Release the rear brake and downshift.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep it locked until you stop completely.
questions.explanation: Keep the rear brake locked until you stop. You can still control your motorcycle if it stays upright and travels straight.

questions.question: Alcohol does not need to be digested like most food and drinks. What does this mean?

options.text: Alcohol reaches the brain within minutes and starts affecting the drinker right away.
It takes a long time to feel the effects of alcohol.
Your body removes alcohol from your system very quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alcohol reaches the brain within minutes and starts affecting the drinker right away.
questions.explanation: Alcohol does not need to be digested. It enters the bloodstream quickly and reaches the brain in minutes. Your body removes about one drink per hour at a slow rate.

questions.question: When a passenger rides on your motorcycle, what should you tell them to do?

options.text: Sit as far back as possible.
Put their feet on the muffler.
Get on the motorcycle after you have started the engine.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get on the motorcycle after you have started the engine.
questions.explanation: Give your passenger safety instructions before you leave. Have them get on only after you start the engine. They should sit forward without crowding you and hold onto your waist, hips, or belt. They must keep both feet on the footrests at all times, even when stopped.

questions.question: If you wait one hour after having one alcoholic drink, can you ride safely?

options.text: You cannot be arrested for drinking and riding.
Your riding skills will not be affected by alcohol.
Alcohol effects may still be in your system.
You will be fine as long as you ride slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alcohol effects may still be in your system.
questions.explanation: Your body removes about one drink per hour. However, alcohol can still build up in your system even if you drink one drink per hour. This buildup can still affect your ability to ride safely.

questions.question: Small vehicles can appear ______ and seem to be traveling ______ than they actually are.
questions.explanation: Small vehicles, like motorcycles, look farther away and seem to move more slowly than they really do. This makes it hard for other drivers to judge where the motorcycle is and how fast it is going.

questions.question: Motorcycle passengers must wear a helmet.
questions.explanation: Helmets reduce the risk of serious head injuries in a crash. However, Illinois law does not require motorcycle passengers to wear them.
